description: Tested-together combinations of the Oscar_Server and Bruno_Collection. The server reads this at startup and surfaces a warning in /v1/health if the running combination is not listed.

notes: feat(ops): every container in the stack (oscar, loki, promtail, grafana, prometheus, alertmanager, autoheal, watchtower) now defaults to Europe/Paris wall-clock time. Was UTC. Affects log timestamps, audit log entries, 'Sent at' lines in emails, run start/finish times rendered in the dashboard. Storage stays UTC ISO-8601 in the JSON layer (correct, unchanged).
Operator override: set OSCAR_TZ=<IANA zone> in .env (e.g. America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo). Defaults to Europe/Paris because that's where the canonical UIC OSCAR deployment is hosted.

Operator action required: pull the latest OSCAR_Deploy/ on the VPS (git pull) and re-up the stack — docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.metrics.yml up -d. Existing containers are recreated with the new TZ env var. Watchtower won't auto-pick this up because the change is in the compose YAML, not the image.

fix(critical #60 Phase 2 follow-up): three file-reader sites still read OSCAR1-encrypted artifacts/datafiles directly via fs.readFileSync, then handed the ciphertext to JSON.parse. Result: 'Could not parse data file: Unexpected token O, "OSCAR1..." is not valid JSON' when a tester re-ran a test config after v1.11.0, or when the dashboard compared two runs. Reported by a Paxone tester after running a test config a second time.

Fixed sites: src/api/routes/runs.js (parallel-mode datafile loader), src/reports/diff.js (Bruno results comparison), src/reports/structureResults.js (Bruno raw results parser). All three now go through utils/at-rest.decryptFromFile() which transparently handles both OSCAR1-encrypted files (post-v1.11.0) and legacy plaintext files (pre-v1.11.0 backfill fall-through).
Operator action required: none. Watchtower picks up :stable automatically. No data migration; the helper transparently handles both file shapes.

fix(ux): batch header rows on the dashboard now show the submitter for test_manager + administrator roles, alongside the per-run submitter subtitle shipped in v1.11.3. A test_manager triaging the queue can now see at a glance who in their team launched each batch, without needing to expand it. Within a batch all runs are submitted by the same user; the header pulls submitted_by from the first child.

feat(ux): dashboard now shows the submitter email under each run label for test_manager and administrator roles. Closes the gap left by Phase 1 (v1.10.0) — test_managers triaging their company's runs need to know who in the team kicked off each one. Testers see only their own runs so the subtitle is redundant for them.

feat(security): test_manager's delete is now a permanent delete (status DELETED), not a soft delete awaiting admin approval. Follow-on to issue #60 Phase 1: administrators no longer read vendor test data, so the soft-delete → admin-review → permanent-delete flow is stale for company-internal cleanups. Test_managers are the data owners for their company and decide directly. Testers still soft-delete (DELETION_REQUESTED) for the safety net.

feat(ux): delete confirmation modal text + button label adapt to user role. Test_managers get a clear ⚠️ warning that the deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Testers continue to see the soft-delete language. Administrators see the flagging language.
Operator action required: none. UI change picked up on next page reload. Existing pending DELETION_REQUESTED runs remain in admin's lifecycle queue.

docs(security #60): vendor data sovereignty Phase 3 — operational policy. Closes the trilogy. Phase 1 was application-level access control (v1.10.0), Phase 2 at-rest encryption (v1.11.0+.1), Phase 3 is the organisational policy that defines who has root SSH on production, how the four long-lived secrets are managed and rotated, backup encryption posture, the SEV-1 incident playbook, and the procedure when a vendor reports data-leak suspicion.

New file: Documentation/Server_Operations/OSCAR - Security Operations Policy.md. Includes a worked example using this morning's v19 migration outage as a concrete SEV-1 case study with timeline + action items.
Admin Guide § 15.5 updated — Phase 3 marked complete, cross-reference to the policy doc.
Operator action required: none. Docs-only release; OSCAR image unchanged in substance (just the version bump). Watchtower's next pull is a no-op.

fix(critical): v19 migration crash on boot, leaving OSCAR in restart-loop. Migration used SELECT rowid + UPDATE WHERE rowid = ?, but Node 22's built-in node:sqlite does not expose rowid as a row property — r.rowid was undefined and binding failed with 'Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 2'. Switched to the explicit `id` primary key (uniform across all four affected tables). Also added per-row error isolation so a single unbindable row doesn't abort the whole table's migration.

Took down production for ~15 minutes when v1.11.0 :stable rolled out via Watchtower; recovered by pinning to the :edge image tag temporarily. v1.11.1 fixes the migration cleanly. v18 was already applied (additive ALTER TABLE columns survive cleanly across version skews).

Operator action after rollover: docker compose pull oscar && docker compose up -d --force-recreate oscar. The v19 migration will then run successfully, encrypting existing plaintext rows on first boot.

feat(security #60): vendor data sovereignty Phase 2 — at-rest encryption. Sensitive content on disk is now AES-256-GCM encrypted using the existing ENCRYPTION_KEY: HTML reports, JSON results, company datafiles, plus the contents of run_events.message, run_requests.{request_body,request_headers,response_body,response_headers,context}, test_frameworks.config, test_resources.data. Anyone running `cat` on the file or `sqlite3 .dump` on the DB sees the OSCAR1 envelope (file) or 'enc:v1:' prefix + base64 ciphertext (column) — never plaintext.

Backward-compat preserved end-to-end: legacy plaintext files (no OSCAR1 magic header) and legacy plaintext rows (no enc:v1: prefix) remain readable forever — the read helpers detect them and pass through unchanged. The v19 migration backfill is idempotent and can be skipped on small instances if desired.

Schema migration v19 — encrypts existing plaintext rows in run_events, run_requests, test_frameworks, test_resources. Per-table transactions; rollback on failure; logs row counts. Idempotent: rows already prefixed are skipped on subsequent runs.

Threat coverage extended: sysadmin running `sudo cat /opt/OSCAR/.../data/oscar.db | strings` now reveals only structural metadata (status, timestamps, http_status, suite_name) — never log content, HTTP traffic, scenarios, or test framework. Same for artifact + datafile reads. The remaining gap is operator-side: a sysadmin attaching a debugger to the running OSCAR process can extract the in-memory key. That's covered by Phase 3 (operational policy doc, no code).

fix(reports): pre-existing latent bug — the /v1/reports/requests/:id/messages endpoint queried four columns (req_body, req_headers, resp_body, resp_headers) that don't exist in the schema (real names are request_*/response_*). The HTTP message viewer in Report Builder was silently empty. Fixed alongside the encryption work since both touch the same query.

Operator action required after rollover: none. v19 migration runs automatically on first boot; existing artifacts and datafiles remain readable as-is. New writes are encrypted. An optional one-time backfill script for existing artifact files lives in OSCAR_Deploy/scripts/encrypt-existing-artifacts.sh — purely cleanup, not required.

feat(security #60): vendor data sovereignty — Phase 1. Introduces a per-run share-with-certifier toggle (replaces the all-or-nothing company-wide flag), strips the administrator role of all read access to test data (test config, datafile, runs, artifacts, assertions), and closes a static-serve bypass that previously let any anonymous user download an artifact knowing only the run UUID.

BREAKING (admin role): administrators can no longer read /v1/runs (per-run content), /v1/runs/:id, /v1/runs/:id/artifacts, /v1/company/test-framework, /v1/company/datafile, /v1/company/test-resources. The role becomes operations + security only (users, companies metadata, server config, alerts, audit log, observability stack). Aggregate run counts remain visible via /v1/admin/activity. Pending-deletion lifecycle queue remains visible (DELETION_REQUESTED + DELETED_BY_ADMIN status only).

BREAKING (certifier visibility): certifiers no longer see all of a vendor's runs based on the company-wide share toggle. They see ONLY runs the test_manager has explicitly shared via the new 'Share with certifiers' button on each run-detail page. The legacy companies.share_reports_with_certifier toggle becomes a master kill switch — when 0, it overrides every per-run share. v18 migration backfills all terminal runs of currently-shared companies as 'shared' so existing certifier workflows don't break on rollover.

fix(critical): /artifacts/<runId>/<filename> and /data/<filename> were served by express.static with no auth — anyone able to reach OSCAR could download artifacts knowing only a run UUID. Both routes now require authenticated session + per-run-ownership check (artifacts) or company-slug match (datafile). Bruno's loopback fetch of /data continues to work via a no-X-Forwarded-For exception.

Schema migration v18 — runs gains shared_with_certifier_at + shared_with_certifier_by columns; partial index on shared_with_certifier_at; backfill of legacy company-wide-share runs. Idempotent and run-once.

Operator action required after rollover: none for the canonical UIC deployment — every existing certifier-visible run is preserved by the v18 backfill. Per-run sharing becomes the model for all NEW runs; test_managers can revoke or extend access run-by-run via the new UI button. Self-hosters: nothing extra.

Threat model (documented in admin guide § 15): defends against admin-browsing-UI access, anonymous artifact bypass, per-company leakage, and certifier overreach. Does NOT defend against root SSH access reading raw oscar.db on disk (Phase 2 — at-rest DB encryption — separate release).

fix(ux #19): Test Config save confirmation is now a fixed-position toast pinned to the top of the viewport regardless of scroll. Previously the in-flow message rendered at the very top of the page so an admin saving from the bottom of the long Test Config form had no visual confirmation that the save succeeded.

feat(ux #18): dashboard batch summary replaces the single 'X/Y done' pill with three side-by-side counters (✓ passed, ✗ failed, ⌛ running) so failures are immediately visible at a glance instead of being hidden behind a deceptive 'progress' wording.
ops: GitHub Action re-renders the Self-Hosted Quick Start PDF whenever its markdown source changes on main and commits the regenerated file back. Eliminates manual PDF regeneration.
Closes #14 (no code change — root cause was misconfigured SMTP_FROM, hardened in v1.9.0 with field renaming + soft-validation warnings + Send test email button).

feat(alerting): unified SMTP + alerting config in the admin UI. Server Config tab gains an Alerting card (ALERT_RECIPIENTS, ALERT_REPEAT_CRITICAL, ALERT_REPEAT_WARNING) plus a one-click 'Apply alerting config' button that templates alertmanager.yml from the same SMTP_* values OSCAR uses, writes it to a shared volume, and hot-reloads Alertmanager via /-/reload — no SSH or VPS file edit needed.

feat(smtp-ux): SMTP fields renamed for clarity (SMTP Login vs Display 'From' Address) with inline help text + soft-validation warnings when SMTP_FROM looks like a relay-internal authentication identity (e.g. *@smtp-brevo.com) or duplicates SMTP_USER. Closes the diagnostic gap that produced the SMTP_USER-pasted-into-SMTP_FROM incident.

feat(auth-ux): global fetch interceptor in nav.js detects 401 from any authenticated API call, clears stale localStorage, and redirects to login with a friendly 'Your session has expired' notice. Replaces the v1.8.1 'dead UI after cookie expiry' state with a clean re-auth flow.

Operator action required after rollover: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.metrics.yml up -d --force-recreate oscar alertmanager (recreates with the new alertmanager-config shared volume). Then in OSCAR Server Config tab → fill in ALERT_RECIPIENTS → Save → click 'Apply alerting config'. The host-edited /opt/OSCAR/OSCAR_Deploy/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml can be deleted after this — it's no longer used.

fix(auth): redirect-loop on welcome.html (and 6 other pages) for users whose session is cookie-only — typically anyone freshly created via the email-verification flow. The auth guards still checked localStorage.oscar_token (the legacy bearer-token model), but the verify-email flow only writes the httpOnly cookie + oscar_user — leaving oscar_token absent and bouncing the page back to / which bounced back to /welcome.html (visible 'blinking' on the welcome banner). Guards now use oscar_user as the session presence proxy; oscar_token is preserved for legacy Bearer-header fetches when present. Affects welcome.html, admin.html, compare.html, dashboard.html, profile.html, run-detail.html, run.html.
Existing administrator sessions were unaffected because they retained oscar_token in localStorage from before the cookie migration.

feat(ops): operational watchdog + email alerting. Docker healthcheck on the OSCAR container probes /health every 30 s; willfarrell/autoheal sidecar restarts any unhealthy container automatically. Prometheus alert rules ship for: oscar down, restart loop, queue stuck, sustained run-failure rate, SMTP degraded, login attack burst, memory leak, event-loop lag. Alertmanager routes firing alerts to admin email via the existing SMTP relay.
feat(ops): two news entries on welcome page — operations monitoring upgrade, and recap of credential redaction + self-service report deletion + password reset by email.

docs: solution architecture (§ 10.1), specification NFRs (§ 5), and admin guide (new §§ 13–14) updated with the full observability + watchdog stack. metrics-and-monitoring.md gets new troubleshooting rows for autoheal + alertmanager.

Operator action required after rollover: (1) cp OSCAR_Deploy/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml.example → alertmanager.yml on the host, fill in SMTP credentials + recipient list. (2) docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.metrics.yml up -d --force-recreate oscar autoheal alertmanager prometheus. Resource cost rises from ~380 MB to ~415 MB RAM. Full guide in Documentation/Server_Operations/OSCAR - Server Admin Guide.md § 14.

feat(loki): centralised log aggregation via Loki + Promtail (PR #52). Admin Dashboard tile 📝 Logs is now live and deep-links to a pre-built 'OSCAR · Logs' Grafana dashboard with errors-only view, full live tail, per-container filter, and ad-hoc search. All container stdout/stderr is shipped automatically — picks up new containers without config changes.

fix(sso): bake the auth_request Host: localhost + X-Forwarded-Proto fix into source nginx snippet (PR #51) — was applied live on the VPS during v1.6.0 rollout. New deployers no longer hit the 500 Internal Server Error on first /grafana/ visit.

Operator action required after rollover: docker compose up -d loki promtail (and recreate grafana) to start the logs stack. Existing metrics stack unaffected. Resource cost rises from ~270 MB to ~380 MB RAM. Full guide in Documentation/Server_Operations/metrics-and-monitoring.md.

feat(sso): Grafana + Prometheus now SSO'd through OSCAR — admin role required, no separate password. New /v1/auth/sso-check endpoint validates the OSCAR JWT cookie and feeds X-WEBAUTH-USER to Grafana's auth.proxy. Replaces the htpasswd basic-auth setup from v1.5.0/v1.5.1.
feat(metrics): Prometheus web UI exposed at /prometheus/ behind same SSO gate. Useful for raw PromQL queries / scrape-target health.
feat(admin-ui): new 'Admin Dashboard' nav entry (admin-only) → /admin-dashboard.html with Grafana / Prometheus / Loki tiles. Loki tile is a placeholder for the next iteration.
fix(metrics): also bakes post-v1.5.0 fixes into source (GF_SERVER_DOMAIN, datasource UID, nginx proxy_pass trailing-slash) so refresh-collection.sh stops failing on dirty working tree.
fix(security): /v1/auth/sso-check rate-limited 600/5min/IP (CodeQL js/missing-rate-limiting).

Operator action required after rollover: replace the OLD nginx /grafana/ block with the new 3-block snippet (auth_request + /grafana/ + /prometheus/), reload nginx, recreate Grafana to pick up new env vars. Full instructions in Documentation/Server_Operations/metrics-and-monitoring.md.

fix(metrics): skip HTTPS-redirect middleware for /metrics. PR #41/v1.5.0 added the endpoint, but PR #7/#23's HTTPS-redirect intercepted Prometheus's docker-internal scrape (400 Bad Request OR 301 → ECONNREFUSED depending on ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS). Now skipped per-path. Operators do NOT need to add 'oscar' to ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS — the standard prometheus.yml shipped in v1.5.0 works as-is.

feat(metrics): Prometheus + Grafana integration (opt-in). New /metrics endpoint exposes Node.js process metrics + OSCAR-specific counters (HTTP duration histogram, runs by status, queue depth, active runs, login attempts, SMTP sends).

Optional metrics stack via OSCAR_Deploy/docker-compose.metrics.yml — Prometheus (15s scrape, 15d retention) + Grafana (with auto-provisioned 10-panel OSCAR Overview dashboard). Grafana served at /grafana/ behind nginx basic auth.
Default deployments unaffected — opt-in via the compose overlay. Resource cost when enabled: ~270 MB RAM + ~550 MB disk (15d).
Operator guide: Documentation/Server_Operations/metrics-and-monitoring.md.

Closes #34 UI gap: dashboard batch header rows now have a select-all checkbox. Click once to select every scenario in the batch (instead of expanding the batch and ticking each scenario individually). Indeterminate gray-dash state when some children are selected. Applies to testers, test_managers, and admins.

Closes #34: test_manager can now soft-delete any run in their own company (matches the elevated privileges they already had over /v1/company/users and the share_reports_with_certifier toggle). Tenant filter still enforces company boundary — cross-company delete remains impossible. Bulk-admin-action (purge) stays administrator-only.

Closes #17 third leak path: per-scenario HTML report at /artifacts/<runId>/report_<scenario>.html now redacts sensitive headers and auth-endpoint bodies (Bruno_Collection/library-bruno/reportGenerator.js, mirrors mergeReport.js + structureResults.js redaction).

Migration v17 retroactive scrub of run_requests is also now in place (was rolled into v1.4.1 via re-applied PR #32). Boot logs show '[db] migration v17 — scrubbed credentials from N of M run_requests rows' once.

Old report_*.html files in /artifacts/ are NOT auto-cleaned (file system, not DB). Optional one-time cleanup: 'sudo find /opt/OSCAR/Oscar_Server/data/artifacts -name report_*.html -delete' (forces re-run of affected scenarios).

Closes #17 server-side leak: structureResults.js now redacts sensitive headers (Authorization, Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key, etc.) and auth-endpoint request/response bodies BEFORE storing in run_requests. New runs never accumulate plaintext credentials.

DB migration v17 retroactively scrubs every existing run_requests row using the same redaction logic. Idempotent. Boot logs show '[db] migration v17 — scrubbed credentials from N of M run_requests rows' once.

Deploy automation: refresh-collection.yml now also fires on compatibility.json changes; promote-release.yml SSHes the VPS after :stable push to refresh the host repo. Eliminates the manual 'ssh + git pull' that was needed after every release.

Closes #15: self-service password reset. Login page gets a 'Forgot password?' link, two new public pages (/forgot-password.html and /reset-password.html), three new public endpoints under /v1/auth/password-reset/*, schema migration v16 (password_reset_tokens table).
Closes #14 diagnostic gap: new admin 'Test SMTP Email' button on Server Config tab — verify SMTP end-to-end with verbatim relay error displayed in the UI, no SSH needed.
Admin escape hatch for #14: 'Reset Link' button on each user row generates a self-service reset URL the admin can deliver out-of-band when SMTP is misconfigured.
UI hardening (#16 follow-up): Token URL, Scope, Requestor Header, Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key inputs are now type=password (visible only as dots while typing).
esc() helper hardened to escape '"' and "'" in addition to & < > — safe for both text and attribute contexts (CodeQL js/incomplete-html-attribute-sanitization, defense in depth on existing buttons).
Auth rate limiting: password-reset/check-token and /confirm now share a 30 / 15 min / IP limiter (CodeQL js/missing-rate-limiting).

Sonar S5146 follow-up: req.url is now validated against a safe-local-path regex before being concatenated into the HTTPS-redirect Location header. Defense in depth on top of the Host: allow-list shipped in 2026.10.
Closes #16: testers can clear stored API credentials. Server-side me-credentials.js now accepts null/empty to wipe a field; profile UI gets a 🗑 Clear all credentials button.
Closes #17: Bruno mergeReport.js redacts sensitive headers (Authorization, X-Subscription-Key, etc.) and auth-endpoint request/response bodies before serialising into downloadable reports.
Bruno collection bumped to OTST_V2.0.2 to record the redaction change.
Trivial fix: trimRight → trimEnd (Sonar S7783).
First release cut via the auto-tag-on-merge automation (Layer 2).
Open-redirect guard in HTTPS middleware (Sonar S5146) — set ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS in .env to activate.
Sonar BUG count 8 → 0 (S3403 / S3923 / S2871 mechanical fixes).
Sonar BLOCKER code-smell count 3 → 0 (explicit expect() in auth-middleware tests, S2699).
Spawn hardening (Sonar S4721): shell:false on Linux, conditional only on Windows .cmd/.bat shims.
Path-traversal guards on all fs calls taking runId (Sonar S6549): central safeJoinUuid helper + inline UUID-regex guard.
DOM-XSS hardening (Sonar S5247): esc() wrappers on all innerHTML template-literal interpolations.
axios bumped to ^1.15.2 in three Bruno-internal locations (top-level + @usebruno/js + @usebruno/requests) — clears 4 HIGH CVEs (CVE-2026-42033, -42035, -42043, -42264).
express-rate-limit bumped to 8.5.1 (ip-address XSS advisory).
Full SAST suite wired in: CodeQL + SonarCloud + Gitleaks + Dependabot, with branch protection enforcing 7 required green checks before merge.
Privacy toggle and Test Manager user-mgmt features carried over from 2026.08 — first release where they ship under the hardened pipeline.
Per-company privacy toggle: 'Share test reports with Certifiers' on the API Config page.
Test Manager user management surface (/v1/company/users) — create / edit / delete / reset-password for users in their own company.
DB schema migration v15: companies.share_reports_with_certifier.
Smoke-test of the auto-deploy pipeline.
Switched Watchtower from containrrr/watchtower (unmaintained) to nickfedor/watchtower active fork.
Adds the version chip to the top banner showing release / server / collection.
Multi-stage Dockerfile drops npm from runtime (clears CVE-2026-33671 picomatch).
HTTP message chain viewer.
